Rashi on Nazir 35a:1:1.hebrew: פרטא מנא ליה - מנא ליה דפרט וכלל ופרט, אי אתה דן אלא כעין הפרט:
Rashi on Nazir 35a:1:1.english: From where does he [derive] the detail? - From where does he [derive] that [in the case of] a detail, a generalization, and a detail, you judge only according to what is similar to the detail?

Rashi on Nazir 35a:1:2.hebrew: סבר ליה כר' אלעזר דדריש ריבויי ומיעוטי - ולא משמע ליה מהאי חרצנים ועד זג פרט, וקא דריש ביה כי טעמיה, שלכך הוא בא: שאינו חייב עד שיאכל כל שני חרצנים וזג:
Rashi on Nazir 35a:1:2.english: He holds in accordance with Rabbi Elazar, who expounds amplifications and restrictions - And it does not indicate to him that this [phrase], “from pits to grape skin,” is a detail; and he expounds it according to his reasoning, that for this [purpose] it comes: that he is not liable until he eats all of two pits and a grape skin.

Rashi on Nazir 35a:2:1.hebrew: ואיבעית אימא דאית ליה כרבנן - דדרשי כללי ופרטי, ואף ע"ג דמשמע ליה מיניה דלפרטא הוא דאתא:
Rashi on Nazir 35a:2:1.english: And if you wish, say that he holds in accordance with the Rabbis - Who expound generalizations and details, and even though it is understood by him from it that it comes as a detail:

Rashi on Nazir 35a:2:2.hebrew: למידייניה בכלל ופרט - ולא משום דר' אלעזר בן עזריה:
Rashi on Nazir 35a:2:2.english: To derive it by a generalization and a detail - And not on account of [the teaching] of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya.

Rashi on Nazir 35a:4:1.hebrew: ולר' אלעזר דדריש ביה ריבויי ומיעוטי פרט וכלל ופרט מנא ליה - דדיינינן כעין הפרט:
Rashi on Nazir 35a:4:1.english: And according to Rabbi Elazar, who interprets it [by means of] amplifications and restrictions, from where does he [derive] a detail, a generalization, and a detail? - That we deduce [items] similar to the detail:

Rashi on Nazir 35a:5:1.hebrew: כי יתן איש אל רעהו חמור או שור או שה פרט וכל בהמה כלל - ואפילו דובים ואריות. ״לשמור״ — חזר ופרט; ״אי אתה דן אלא כעין הפרט״ — דאהני פרטא בתרא: למידי דבר שמירה הוא דנשבעין עליהן, כגון נמי עופות; יצאו דובים ואריות, דלאו בני שמירה נינהו, שאין להם תרבות:
Rashi on Nazir 35a:5:1.english: “If a man deliver to his neighbor a donkey, or an ox, or a sheep” — a detail; “and any animal” — a generalization - And [this includes] even bears and lions. “[The word] to guard” — it detailed again; “you deduce only [items] similar to the detail” — for the latter detail is effective [in teaching that] it is [only] concerning an item capable of being guarded that an oath is taken, such as birds as well; excluded are bears and lions, which are not capable of being guarded, as they are not domesticated.

Rashi on Nazir 35a:6:1.english: Rava said: From this verse - “And if his offering is from the flock, from the sheep or from the goats, for a burnt offering, a male without blemish he shall offer it” (Leviticus 1:10).

Rashi on Nazir 35a:6:2.hebrew: מן פרט הצאן כלל - ואפי' רובע ונרבע, מוקצה ונעבד, ואתנן ומחיר — שכשרין לקרבן:
Rashi on Nazir 35a:6:2.english: “From” is a detail; “the flock” is a generalization - And even an animal that copulated [with a human] or was copulated with, [an animal] set aside [for idolatry] or worshipped, and the hire [of a harlot] and the price [of a dog] — that they are fit for an offering.

Rashi on Nazir 35a:6:3.hebrew: מן הכשבים ומן העזים חזר ופרט - דלא משמע ליה כללא כמו צאן, ואימעיטו להו כל הני, ואיתרבו לה כגון נעבדה בהם עבירה, כגון החורש בשור ובחמור ושחרש בו בשבת:
Rashi on Nazir 35a:6:3.english: “From the sheep and from the goats,” it has detailed again - For this does not imply to him a general term like “flock”; and all those [disqualifications] are excluded, and [animals] such as [those with which] a transgression was committed are included, such as [an animal used by] one who plows with an ox and a donkey, or [an animal] with which one plowed on Shabbat.

Rashi on Nazir 35a:8:1.hebrew: ולילף מן הדין קרא - "מן הבהמה ומן הבקר ומן הצאן יקריבנו". "מן" — פרט, דמשמע: "מן הבהמה" ולא כל בהמה. "הבהמה" — כלל, אפילו חיה, דחיה בכלל בהמה, כו':
Rashi on Nazir 35a:8:1.english: And let him derive [it] from this verse - [The verse states:] “From the animal, from the herd, and from the flock, he shall offer it.” “From” is a detail, as it implies: “From the animal,” and not all animals. “The animal” is a generalization, [including] even a wild beast, for a wild beast is included in [the category of] “animal,” etc.

Rashi on Nazir 35a:8:2.hebrew: ואיבעית אימא דאית ליה כרבנן - דדרשי כללי ופרטי, ואף ע"ג דמשמע ליה מיניה, דלפרטא הוא דאתא:
Rashi on Nazir 35a:8:2.english: And if you wish, say that he holds in accordance with the Rabbis - who expound generalizations and details; and even though he derives [his teaching] from it, [nevertheless] it came to serve as a detail:

Tosafot on Nazir 35a:1:1.hebrew: שני חרצנים שבאים בתוך הענב וזג [א'] - מן הקליפה. החרצנים — לאפוקי שאם אכל כזית מן החרצנים, או כזית מן הזגין, אינו חייב; עד שיאכל הגרעינין והקליפה החיצונה:
Tosafot on Nazir 35a:1:1.english: "Two grape seeds" [are those] that come from inside the grape, and [one] "grape skin" - [is] from the peel. "The grape seeds" — [this comes] to exclude [the view of the Rabbis, teaching] that if he ate an olive-bulk of the grape seeds or an olive-bulk of the grape skins he is not liable, until he eats [both] the seeds and the outer peel.

Tosafot on Nazir 35a:1:2.hebrew: סבר לה כר' אלעזר דדריש רבויי ומיעוטי - ורבי אלעזר נמי כר"א בן עזריה דריש, ולא למעוטי — כדפ"ל:
Tosafot on Nazir 35a:1:2.english: He holds in accordance with Rabbi Elazar, who expounds amplifications and restrictions - And Rabbi Elazar also expounds [this verse] in accordance with Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya, and not to restrict [the prohibition], as explained above.

Tosafot on Nazir 35a:2:1.hebrew: ואיבעית אימא כרבנן - ושפיר אית ליה לר"א [ב"ע] מלתייהו דרבנן, ותרתי שמעי' מינה: דאי ס"ד לכדר"א [ב"ע] לחודיה — לכתוב רחמנא "מחרצנים ועד זג" לגבי פרטי קודם הכלל; ואי לדרשא דפרט וכלל ופרט כדרבנן לחודיה אתו — לכתוב או "חרצנים (או שני) וזגין", או "חרצן וזג", שניהם בלשון רבים או שניהם בלשון יחיד. אלא ש"מ כר' אלעזר ב"ע:
Tosafot on Nazir 35a:2:1.english: And if you wish, say [that he holds] in accordance with the Rabbis - And Rabbi Elazar [ben Azarya] indeed accepts the position of the Rabbis, and two things we deduce from it: For if it should enter your mind that [the phrase comes] for that of Rabbi Elazar [ben Azarya] alone, let the Merciful One write "from pits to grape skin" alongside the details before the generalization; and if it comes for the exposition of a detail, a generalization, and a detail in accordance with the Rabbis alone, let it write either "pits (or: two) and skins" or "a pit and a skin" — both of them in the plural or both of them in the singular. Rather, conclude from it [both expositions, in accordance with the Rabbis and] in accordance with Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya.

Tosafot on Nazir 35a:4:1.hebrew: ורבי אלעזר דדריש ריבה ומיעט פרט וכלל ופרט מנליה - וא"ת: ודלמא לית ליה [המדה] בשום מקום, כי היכי דרבנן לא דרשי מיעט וריבה? וי"ל: דא"כ, הוה לו לחלוק בכ"מ שאנו דורשין בכלל ופרט וכלל ומרבינן מההוא ריבוי כעין הפרט, כמו קרא דוכי יתן דבסמוך, דרבנן דרשי ליה בכלל ופרט וכלל בהזהב בב"מ (ד' נז:) לרבות כעין הפרט — דבר שמיטלטל וגופו ממון, ולהוציא שטרות וקרקעות ועבדים; ולא מצינו שר' אלעזר חולק על מדות הללו וריבה יותר מריבה ומיעט, אלא גם הוא מודה שאין נשבעין על הקרקעות והשטרות ועבדים. ומש"ה פשיטא ליה לגמרא כי במקום שאנו דורשין כלל ופרט וכלל, ידרוש הוא פרט וכלל ופרט אם יכול להפיל כלל הראשון, ואם אינו יכול — אז דורשו בריבה ומיעט וריבה, שכך קבל המדות. וכשהוא דורש פרט וכלל ופרט מרבה כעין הפרט כמו רבנן בכלל ופרט וכלל (במשמע דרשא להאי קרא ר' יוסי אומר דבסמוך), אך קצת יש חילוק ביניהם לרבנן כדמפרש בסמוך. א"נ [אומר ר"י], דע"כ אית ליה בעלמא פרט וכלל ופרט; דאי הוי דריש במיעט וריבה ומיעט, ס"ל לגמרא דגם גבי נזיר הוה דריש ליה במיעט וריבה ומיעט, ולא הוה דריש מיעוט אחרון לכדר' אלעזר ב"ע, דהכי עדיף; אלא ודאי [כדפרישית], דמדה דמיעט וריבה ומיעט לא דריש ליה, אלא דריש ליה בפרט וכלל, לפי דמדה דמיעט וריבה ומיעט אינו מדה בתורה לידרש. וכ"ת: אכתי, כיון דבעלמא דריש פרט וכלל ופרט, ה"נ גבי נזיר לידרשיה כרבנן? ויש לומר: הואיל דבעלמא דריש כל התורה בריבה ומיעט, וכן במיעט וריבה, וכן בריבה ומיעט וריבה, ואף דפרט וכלל ופרט ניתן לידרש — הואיל דברוב מקומות לא ניתן כלל ופרט לידרש, נוח לו לדרוש פרט אחרון לכדר' אלעזר מלדרשו לפרט וכלל ופרט; אך כשאין לו מה לדרוש מפרט אחרון דרשא אחרינא, אז דורשין בפרט וכלל ופרט:
Tosafot on Nazir 35a:4:1.english: “And Rabbi Elazar, who interprets [via] amplification and restriction, from where does he [derive] a detail, a generalization, and a detail?” - And if you say: But perhaps he does not accept [this hermeneutical measure] anywhere, just as the Rabbis do not interpret [via] restriction and amplification? And one can say: For if so, he should have disputed in every place where we interpret via a generalization, a detail, and a generalization, and include from that inclusion [items] similar to the detail — such as the verse of “And if a man deliver…” (Exodus 22:9) mentioned nearby, which the Rabbis interpret via a generalization, a detail, and a generalization in [the chapter entitled] HaZahav in Bava Metzia (57b), to include [items] similar to the detail: that which is movable and has intrinsic monetary value, and to exclude deeds, land, and [Canaanite] slaves. And we do not find that Rabbi Elazar disputes these hermeneutical measures and amplifies [to include] more [items, as would result] from [the method of] amplification and restriction; rather, he too admits that one does not take an oath regarding land, deeds, and slaves. And for this reason, it was obvious to the Gemara that in a place where we interpret [via] a generalization, a detail, and a generalization, he would interpret [via] a detail, a generalization, and a detail if he can set aside the first generalization; and if he cannot, he then interprets it via amplification, restriction, and amplification, for that is how he received the traditions of the hermeneutical measures. And when he interprets [via] a detail, a generalization, and a detail, he includes [items] similar to the detail, just like the Rabbis [do] in [interpreting via] a generalization, a detail, and a generalization (as is understood from the exposition of this verse, as Rabbi Yose says nearby); however, there is a slight difference between them and the Rabbis, as [the Gemara] explains nearby. Alternatively, [says the Ri], perforce he accepts [the method of] a detail, a generalization, and a detail generally; for if he interpreted via restriction, amplification, and restriction, the Gemara reasoned that in the case of a nazirite as well he would have interpreted it via restriction, amplification, and restriction, and would not have interpreted the final restriction for [the exposition] like that of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya, as that [interpreting the entire verse through a uniform hermeneutical rule] is preferable. Rather, certainly, [as I explained,] he does not interpret by the measure of restriction, amplification, and restriction, but rather interprets it via a detail and a generalization, because the measure of restriction, amplification, and restriction is not a hermeneutical measure in the Torah to be applied. And if you say: Still, since generally he interprets [via] a detail, a generalization, and a detail, here too regarding a nazirite let him interpret it like the Rabbis? And one can say: Since generally he interprets the entire Torah via amplification and restriction, and similarly via restriction and amplification, and similarly via amplification, restriction, and amplification; and even though [the method of] a detail, a generalization, and a detail may be applied, since in most places [the method of] a generalization and a detail is not applied [by him], it was more preferable to him to interpret the final detail for [the exposition] like that of Rabbi Elazar [ben Azarya] than to interpret it as a detail, a generalization, and a detail. However, when he has no other exposition to derive from the final detail, then one interprets via a detail, a generalization, and a detail.

Tosafot on Nazir 35a:5:1.hebrew: וכי יתן איש אל רעהו חמור או שור או שה פרט - דיתן לא משמע כללא לר' אלעזר, דמה יתן? דהכתוב לא פירש בכלל כלום. על כן הוא מפיל כלל הראשון: דיתן על חמור ושור ושה קאי, דהיינו פרט; וכל — כלל, דמשמע על כל דבר בהמה; לשמור — חזר ופרט. ורבנן דרשי ליה בפרק הזהב בכלל ופרט וכלל. וכן בכל דוכתי דאשכחן דרשא כלל ופרט וכלל דלא פליג ר"א, היינו משום דדריש ליה בפרט וכלל ופרט, וממעט מיניה [דלאו] כעין הפרט, כמו רבנן מכלל ופרט וכלל:
Tosafot on Nazir 35a:5:1.english: “And if a man deliver to his neighbor a donkey, or an ox, or a sheep” is a detail - For [the word] yitein [“shall deliver”] does not imply a generalization according to Rabbi Elazar, for what does he deliver? The verse did not specify anything at all in the generalization. Therefore, he sets aside the first generalization, [explaining] that yitein refers to “a donkey, or an ox, or a sheep,” which is a detail; and “all” [in “or any animal”] is a generalization, as it implies any type of animal; and “to guard” is a detail once again. And the Rabbis expound it in the chapter [entitled] HaZahav as a generalization, a detail, and a generalization. And similarly, in all places where we find an exposition of a generalization, a detail, and a generalization where Rabbi Elazar does not disagree, that is because he expounds it as a detail, a generalization, and a detail, and excludes from it [that which is not] similar to the detail, just as the Rabbis [do] from a generalization, a detail, and a generalization.

Tosafot on Nazir 35a:6:1.hebrew: רבא אמר נפקא ליה מהאי - כלומר, גם בהאי קרא דריש רבי אלעזר פרט וכלל ופרט: "ואם מן הצאן קרבנו מן הכשבים או מן העזים לעולה זכר תמים יקריבנו". "מן" — פרט, דמשמע מקצת צאן ולא כל [צאן]; "צאן" — כלל; "כבשים" "ועזים" — חזר ופרט; ה"ל פרט וכלל ופרט. וי"מ דפרטא משמע למעוטי רובע ונרבע, ויש במשמע למעוטי חורש בשור וחמור וחוסם פי פרה ודש בה, דהשתא נדרוש הכי: מה הפרט מפורש שלא נעבדה בהן עבירה בגופן, ויצא רובע ונרבע שפסולין לקרבן, ומכללא נרבי חורש בשור וחמור וחוסם פי פרה, דלא נעבדה בהן עבירה בגופן. [ואדרבה] קשה: דהיכי משמע מן הפרט למעוטי נעבדה בהן עבירה בגופן? דהכי מקרי כבשים ועזים אי נרבעו כמו לא נרבעו! וע"ק, דרובע ונרבע נפקא לן מקרא אחרינא דפסולין להקרבה! לכך נראה, דמן הפרט משמע למעט שתי שנים, דסתם כבש משמע בן שנה, וסתם עז משמע בת שנתה; וכן בעל מום, דכתיב בפ' "זכר תמים". והשתא שמעינן: מכעין הפרט — בעל מום, ונרבי מהכלל אפילו ב' שנים:
Tosafot on Nazir 35a:6:1.english: Rava said: He derives it from this - That is to say, from this verse as well Rabbi Elazar expounds [using the method of] a detail, a generalization, and a detail: "And if his offering is from the flock, whether of the sheep or of the goats, for a burnt-offering, he shall offer it a male without blemish" (Leviticus 1:10). "From" is a detail, which implies part of the flock and not all [the flock]; "the flock" is a generalization; "sheep" and "goats" — the Torah detailed again; this is a detail, a generalization, and a detail. And some explain that the detail implies the exclusion of [an animal that] copulated [with a human] or [an animal that] was copulated with, and there is in the implication [of the exclusion] to exclude [even an animal used by] one who plows with an ox and a donkey, or one who muzzles the mouth of a cow and threshes with it, so that now we would expound as follows: Just as the detail is explicit [in referring to an animal] with whose body no transgression was committed, and [thus] an animal that copulated or was copulated with is excluded, as they are disqualified for an offering, and from the generalization we include [an animal used by] one who plows with an ox and a donkey, or one who muzzles the mouth of a cow, with whose body no transgression was committed. [On the contrary,] it is difficult: How does the detail imply excluding [an animal] with whose body a transgression was committed? For they are called "sheep" and "goats" whether they were copulated with or they were not copulated with! And furthermore, it is difficult: for that an animal that copulated or was copulated with is disqualified from sacrifice is derived by us from another verse! Therefore, it appears that from the detail, the implication is to exclude [an animal that is] two years [old], for an unspecified "sheep" implies [an animal that is] one year old, and an unspecified "goat" implies [an animal that is] in its first year; and similarly [the detail implies excluding] a blemished animal, as it is written in the section, "a male without blemish." And now we deduce: from that which is similar to the detail — [we exclude] a blemished animal, and from the generalization we include even [an animal that is] two years [old].

Tosafot on Nazir 35a:8:1.hebrew: ולילף מהאי קרא - שהיא פרשה ראשונה, ולמה לא אמר שר"א ידרוש שם פרט וכלל ופרט: "מן" — פרט, דמשמע מקצת בהמה ולא כל בהמה, למעוטי חיה, דבהמה בכלל חיה וחיה בכלל בהמה; "בקר וצאן" — חזר ופרט, דחיה אינו בכלל בקר וצאן. (חזר ופרט) הרי אתה דן כעין הפרט: מה הפרט מפורש — למעוטי חיה מקרבן. ותימה: [כלל] מה אהני? הא לא מרבינן מידי מכעין הפרט! ותירץ מהר"ף: דאהני כללא לרבויי שור [הבר], דבהמה הוא; אף על גב דרגיל בין החיות והוי כעין חיה, אפ"ה כשר לקרבן:
Tosafot on Nazir 35a:8:1.english: And let him derive [it] from this verse - As it is the first section, so why did [Rava] not say that Rabbi Elazar should expound "a detail, a generalization, and a detail" there? [Namely:] "From" is a detail, as it implies part of an animal and not all animals, to exclude a wild beast, for [the term] "beast" includes a wild beast and a wild beast includes a beast; "herd and flock" detailed again, as a wild beast is not included in "herd and flock." (Detailed again.) Behold, you deduce only [items] similar to the detail: just as the detail is explicitly defined, to exclude a wild beast from an offering. But it is astonishing: What did the [generalization] accomplish? For we do not include anything from "similar to the detail"! And Maharaf answered that the generalization served to include the [wild] ox, for it is a domesticated animal; even though it is accustomed [to dwell] among wild beasts and is similar to a wild beast, even so, it is fit for an offering.

Tosafot on Nazir 35a:9:1.hebrew: א"ל מהא ליכא למשמע - מיעוטא דחיה. ד"מן בהמה" לא משמע למעוטי חיה, שהרי חיה בכלל בהמה, והוי כאילו כתיב "מן הבהמה ומן החיה"; ואף על גב ד"מן" משמע מיעוטא, לא ממעט חיה מינה:
Tosafot on Nazir 35a:9:1.english: He said to him: “From this, one cannot derive” - [Namely,] the exclusion of a wild animal. For “from animals” does not imply the exclusion of a wild animal, as a wild animal is included in [the category of] animals, and it is as though it is written: “From domesticated animals and from wild animals”; and even though “from” implies an exclusion, it does not exclude a wild animal from it.
